# AgentBus: the API for agents

> AgentBus runs coding agents (Claude Code, codex, Antigravity, OpenCode, Gemini CLI) for a person and records every step.
> This page is short on purpose: read it whole. The full description of every route, and the
> contract, is `GET /api/v0/openapi.json` (`/docs` shows it as a page).

## Three nouns

- **Agent**: a saved setup: a harness (claude, codex, agy, opencode, gemini), its model, a name. `GET /api/v0/agents`.
- **Session**: one conversation: its turns, in order.
- **Turn**: one message, its reply and its changes. Every action is on a turn.

A turn exists from the moment it is asked for. Its `state` is `queued`, `running`, `finished`,
`failed` or `stopped`. Its `number` is its place in its session: turn 3 is the session's third.

## Your copy and the person's folder

A turn usually works in its workspace's own **copy** of the person's folder. Its edits stay in the
copy. They reach the **person's folder** only when the workspace is **applied**:
`POST /api/v0/workspaces/{id}/apply`. That writes the workspace's unapplied changes; an optional
`{"turn"}` in the body applies only up to that turn, and no body applies up to its latest change.

## Calling the API from a turn

A claude or codex turn may have the apps as tools of its own (when `[agent_api] tools = true`),
from the MCP server `agentbus` at `POST /api/v0/mcp`: `ask_agent`, and any other app. Each does what
its route below does, with your turn's token. Reading the record (turns, diffs, sessions, saved
agents), reviewing, applying and stopping a turn are the API's own routes, reached with
`agentbus-api` (below), not tools.

Your environment has `AGENTBUS_URL` and `AGENTBUS_TOKEN` (your turn's own token; never print it).
Without the tools, use `agentbus-api METHOD PATH [JSON]`: it is on your PATH and sends the token for you.

```sh
agentbus-api GET /api/v0/turns                      # this session's turns, newest first
agentbus-api GET /api/v0/turns/T                    # one turn: state, cost, a review's verdict
agentbus-api POST /api/v0/workspaces/W/apply        # put the workspace's changes in the person's folder
agentbus-api POST /api/v0/turns/T/review '{"agent":"<agent id>"}'
agentbus-api POST /api/v0/turns/T/stop              # stop a queued or running turn
agentbus-api GET /api/v0/turns/T/diff               # a turn's summary: counts, cost, apply state
agentbus-api GET /api/v0/turns/T/changes            # a page of the turn's changed files
agentbus-api GET "/api/v0/sessions/S/search?q=cache" # search a session's history
agentbus-api POST /api/v0/turns '{"agent":"<agent id>","prompt":"..."}'  # ask another agent
```

`T` is a turn id (`t_` and 16 hex digits). `S` is a session id. `W` is a workspace id (`ws_` and 16
hex digits), from `GET /api/v0/workspaces`. Your token reads your own session,
the person's session you came from, and every session work from it started. It reads a turn of
those by its id alone.

## The routes an agent uses

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v0/agents` | The saved agents. Use an agent's `id`. |
| `GET /api/v0/turns` | Turns, newest first; queued ones first. Facts only — no prompt or reply text. `?session=` picks a session (yours by default). |
| `GET /api/v0/turns/{id}` | One turn in any state, with its whole `prompt` and `reply` (read from the record): also `state`, `number`, `cost_usd`; for a review `verdict` and `findings`. |
| `POST /api/v0/turns` | Ask another agent: `{"agent","prompt"}` always opens a new session on its own copy. Your token cannot continue a session: to follow up, ask again. |
| `POST /api/v0/turns/{id}/review` | Ask another agent to review a turn: `{"agent"}`. It starts a review turn. Pick an agent other than the turn's own. |
| `POST /api/v0/workspaces/{id}/apply` | Put the workspace's unapplied changes into the person's folder (optional `{"turn"}` in the body applies up to that turn). A 409 lists each file that changed there, and writes nothing. |
| `POST /api/v0/turns/{id}/stop` | Stop a queued or running turn. It then reads `stopped`. |
| `GET /api/v0/workspaces/{id}/changes` | A page of what applying the workspace's changes would do to the person's folder now: files with diffs against it, and conflicts. Writes nothing. The preview is stored and reused; `?fresh=true` takes a new one, `?before=` and `?event=` page the same one. |
| `GET /api/v0/turns/{id}/diff` | A turn's summary: its agent and timing, how many files it changed, its model and tool call counts (with cost), and apply state. Each list is on its own paged route below. |
| `GET /api/v0/turns/{id}/changes` | A page of the turn's changed files, each with its diff. `?before=` of the previous page's `next_before` for the next page. |
| `GET /api/v0/turns/{id}/calls` | A page of the turn's model calls: model, status, cost, latency. Pages like changes. |
| `GET /api/v0/turns/{id}/tools` | A page of the turn's tool calls, each with the commands it ran. Pages like changes. |
| `GET /api/v0/turns/{id}/calls/{call}` | One model call of the turn, piece by piece. |
| `GET /api/v0/turns/{id}/context` | How full the turn's context got against the model's window and where this harness compacts (`window`), how much came from the prompt cache, and what its largest prompt was made of (`made_of`). |
| `GET /api/v0/sessions/{id}/events?turn=` | A session's events, oldest first; `turn` keeps one turn's. |
| `GET /api/v0/sessions/{id}/search?q=` | Search a session's history. Each hit's `read` is a path to GET. Your own turn is left out. |
| `GET /api/v0/sessions/{id}/context` | A session's context: its token totals and how big each turn's context got, newest first — how the context grows. |

## Asking other agents

Do not wait for work you ask for. Start it, say so, and end your turn. **Each result comes back
to your session as a later turn**, whose prompt starts `[AgentBus] This message is from AgentBus`.
It names the agent, the turn, its state, the changed files, a review's verdict, and the reply.

AgentBus agents are not your harness's own agents or subagents. To have another agent check your
work, ask for a review of your turn, then end your turn.

## Refusals

A 403 says why: a session outside your tree; sending
`"session"` to continue one (your token never continues a session); a folder outside yours; a call the person switched off in
`[agent_api]` of the settings; a limit in `[limits]` (depth 2, 10 asks per turn, 30 per tree
by default). A 404 means no such turn, session or agent. Errors are JSON: `{"error":"..."}`.
